result.title: Accounting Policy Manual - posting authority, support, approvals
result.text:
HALVARD SYSTEMS - ACCOUNTING POLICY MANUAL (excerpt), effective 2026-01-01
Applies to Halvard Systems Inc. (US), Halvard Systems Ltd (UK), Halvard Systems GmbH (DE).

1. Posting authority. Senior accountants may post manual journal entries up to USD 10,000
   per entry (local-currency entries are measured at the month-end rate of the entry month).
   Any entry above USD 10,000 must be routed to the Controller with an approval request
   (request_approval) immediately after posting; it remains pending until approved.
   Splitting one transaction into several entries to stay under the threshold is prohibited.
2. Support. Every journal entry must have its supporting document(s) attached. An entry
   without support is not a valid entry.
3. Capitalization. Individual equipment purchases of USD 2,500 or more (local-currency
   equivalent at the month-end rate) are capitalized to 1500 Computer Equipment and
   depreciated over 36 months beginning the month after acquisition.
4. Prepaids. Payments covering services or events in future periods (more than one month
   out, or spanning more than one month) above USD 1,000 are recorded as prepaid (1210
   Prepaid Software for software, 1220 Prepaid Insurance for insurance, 1200 Prepaid Expenses
   for everything else, including deposits for future events) and expensed straight-line over
   the coverage period starting the month coverage begins, or when the event occurs.
5. Accruals. Expenses are recorded in the period the goods or services are received. Services
   received but not yet invoiced at month-end are accrued to 2100 Accrued Expenses using the
   best available evidence (vendor statements, approved timesheets, engagement terms).
   Quotes or proposals for future work are not liabilities.
6. Revenue. Revenue is recognized under ASC 606 per the contract terms. Deferred revenue
   (2200) is released as performance obligations are satisfied. Usage earned but not yet
   invoiced is recorded to 1300 Unbilled Receivables.
7. Customer credits. SLA credits are issued only per contract terms and verified uptime data
   (see the monthly uptime report). Credits are recorded as a reduction of the related revenue.
8. Cash application. Customer receipts are applied to invoices per remittance advice. Receipts
   that cannot be matched to an open invoice remain in 2950 Unapplied Cash.
9. FX. Monetary balances denominated in a currency other than the entity's functional
   currency are remeasured at the month-end rate; gains/losses go to 6950 FX Gain/Loss.
   Intercompany charges are recorded by the receiving entity at the month-end rate of the
   month charged.
10. Payroll. Returned payroll deposits are recorded to 2150 Accrued Payroll & Unclaimed
   Wages until reissued. Unpaid wages at month-end are accrued to 2150.
11. Exceptions. Items that cannot be supported must be reported via flag_exception. Never
   post an entry to force a reconciliation or to make balances agree.
12. Periods. January and February 2026 are closed. March 2026 is open.

ASC 606 milestone revenue recognition for Evergreen Bank M1, supported by signed customer acceptance certificate dated 2026-03-14 (DOC-0184) and the milestone SOW (DOC-0047). Releases part of the USD 60,000 non-refundable advance held in 2200.

args.text:
MEMO - March 2026 Close
To: Controller
From: David Murguia, Senior Accountant
Date: 2026-04-03
Subject: Evergreen Bank implementation - March 2026 revenue recognition (US entity, ASC 606)

CONCLUSION
Recognized USD 36,000 of professional services revenue in March 2026 for Milestone M1 only. No revenue recognized for M2 or M3.

ENTRY POSTED
JE-00305, US, 2026-03-31, USD 36,000
  Dr 2200 Deferred Revenue        36,000.00
  Cr 4200 Professional Services Revenue  36,000.00
Memo: Evergreen Bank implementation - recognize M1 Solution design revenue on customer acceptance 2026-03-14 (30% x USD 120,000 SOW); release from deferred revenue advance.
Support attached: DOC-0047 (SOW), DOC-0184 (signed M1 acceptance certificate), DOC-0049 (INV-1030 50% advance), DOC-0199 (PM M2 status email).
Approval: entry exceeds the USD 10,000 senior accountant posting limit (Policy Manual §1), so approval was requested immediately after posting. Status: pending_approval.

ANALYSIS AND REASONING
1. Contract / performance obligations (DOC-0047). Fixed fee USD 120,000 under a milestone SOW. The SOW states each deliverable "is distinct and separately accepted," so M1 (30% / 36,000), M2 (50% / 60,000) and M3 (20% / 24,000) are treated as three separate performance obligations, with the stated milestone fees used as the allocated transaction price (contractually stated, commensurate with the distinct deliverables).

2. Timing - point in time, not over time. The SOW states the customer "has no obligation to pay for, and obtains no rights to, a deliverable before acceptance." That defeats the ASC 606-25-27(c) over-time criterion: there is no enforceable right to payment for performance completed to date, and the customer does not control the asset as it is created. Revenue is therefore recognized at the point in time control transfers - i.e., on written customer acceptance, which is also the explicit revenue term in the SOW.

3. M1 - earned. Signed acceptance certificate from D. Whitfield, VP Operations, Evergreen Bank, dated 2026-03-14 (DOC-0184), accepting the M1 deliverable in full. Acceptance occurred in the March period, so USD 36,000 is earned and recognized in March.

4. M2 - NOT earned. The PM status email dated 2026-03-27 (DOC-0199) reports M2 build ~80% complete, customer UAT not started, nothing signed, acceptance targeted for late April. Under the contract terms above, percentage of completion is not an acceptable measure here: no acceptance means no transfer of control and no enforceable right to payment. Recognizing 80% x 60,000 = 48,000 would be incorrect. Recognized USD 0. Expect M2 (USD 60,000) to be recognized in the period the signed acceptance is obtained (likely April 2026).

5. M3 - not started, no revenue (USD 24,000 remaining).

6. No contract asset. Because the customer has no obligation to pay before acceptance, the unaccepted M2 work in progress is not an unconditional or conditional right to consideration; nothing was recorded to 1300 Unbilled Receivables.

7. Cash / deferred revenue mechanics. The customer paid a non-refundable 50% advance of USD 60,000 in January (INV-1030, paid 2026-01-20; recorded as deferred revenue in JE-00072). The advance exceeds the M1 fee, so M1 was recognized entirely by releasing deferred revenue - no new receivable was booked and no additional invoice is required for this entry. Billing of the remaining contract balance is a separate AR matter.

BALANCE ROLLFORWARD (US)
2200 Deferred Revenue: 60,000 Cr before -> 36,000 Dr release -> 24,000 Cr at 3/31/2026. The remaining 24,000 is the unearned portion of the advance and will be applied against M2 on acceptance.
4200 Professional Services Revenue: March activity 7,500 (other projects) + 36,000 = 43,500; YTD 58,500 Cr.

EXCEPTIONS
None flagged. The M2 question is a judgment resolved by the contract's acceptance clause and documented above rather than an unsupported item; no entry was forced.

OPEN ITEMS
- JE-00305 remains pending your approval.
- US "Revenue recognition" checklist item set to in_progress: this memo covers only the Evergreen Bank implementation project. Subscription, usage/unbilled and any SLA credit work for March is still outstanding under that item.
- Follow up in April for the signed M2 acceptance certificate to release the remaining USD 24,000 advance and bill/recognize the balance of M2.
